meta.name: RR Clutch Index
how_to_use: What the score is: who has already delivered when a ball could swing the match, how sure we are, and who has not.
What it is not: a forecast. Tested one season ahead, it did not beat simple stats (strike rate/economy) or a random pick.
How to use it: build the shortlist and set walk-away prices from it, then decide on form, fitness, role and price.
meta.thesis: Back players whose quality has held up when the match was on the line, and know how sure we are.

kpi.claim: Historical pressure-performance indicator; persistence not demonstrated. Its ability to predict IPL 2027 is not established (D15).
exec_summary: We rated 110 players (47 batters and 71 bowlers, 8 of them all-rounders rated both ways) on how they performed when a ball could swing the match (IPL 2023–26).
RR's weakest areas under pressure: middle-overs batting, death-overs batting. These gaps are directional (within statistical noise); RR's bowling is at or above league in every phase.
Must-Back if available: Ashutosh Sharma, Patrick Cummins. Plan A (assumed Rs 15 cr purse; Rs 8.3 cr at mid prices, Rs 13 cr at walk-away): Patrick Cummins, Ashutosh Sharma, Sameer Rizvi.
Honest test (top 10 still above average next season): batters 42.9% v naive 46.7% v random pick 50.8%; bowlers 72.8% v 75.0% v 59.5%. Verdict: persistence not demonstrated.
So read it as proof of past pressure performance, not a promise; prices, ages and availability are unverified assumptions to recheck before 16 Dec.

glossary.meaning: How much a ball could swing the match result, ranked against earlier balls; 80+ = High pressure.
The expected size of the win-probability swing on a ball, given what usually happens in that situation.
The batting side's chance of winning before a ball, from a model trained on earlier seasons only.
How much a player's ball changed his team's chance of winning (in percentage points).
Runs scored minus what an average batter would score on the same balls in the same situations.
Runs an average bowler would concede on the same balls minus the runs actually conceded.
Pulling small samples toward the average so a few lucky balls can't top a ranking.
The range we are 80% sure the true value sits in, from resampling the player's matches.
Share of seasons (with ≥30 High-pressure balls) in which the player was above expected.
0–100 historical pressure-performance indicator within role; roughly a percentile. Not a forecast.
Score built from earlier seasons only, then checked against the next season's pressure performance.
Two players whose 80% ranges overlap: the data can't say who is better.
A value the data can't supply and the web couldn't verify here; stated with its reason.

cutoffs.rule: High = 80+ (about the top 20% of earlier balls), Medium = 50-80, Low = below 50 (D18/D27)

pressure.formula: Pressure = leverage × (1 + 0.1·chase pressure + 0.1·below par + 0.1·death + 0.1·playoff + 0.1·collapse), ranked 0–100 against earlier balls only
explain: Every ball gets a win probability for the batting side, from a model that has only seen earlier seasons.
Leverage = how much that probability could swing on this ball, weighted by what usually happens.
Ranked against earlier balls: 80+ = High (about the top 20%), 50–80 = Medium, below 50 = Low.

flow: Data: 367 IPL matches 2022–26, ball by ball; 2022 used only to train.
Win probability: simple logistic model per season, trained only on earlier seasons.
Pressure Index: how much each ball can swing the result (leverage), plus small context boosts, ranked 0–100 against earlier balls only.
Fair comparison: runs above (batters) or saved (bowlers) versus an average player in the same situation, from earlier matches only.
Reliability: small samples pulled toward average (shrinkage), recent seasons weighted more, 80% ranges by resampling matches.
Clutch score 0–100: frozen weights, percentile-like scale within role; backtested against a naive ranking.
method.formula: Score = 100 × Φ( Σ w·z / sd ) with z = standardised, shrunk component among scorable players of the role; pre-registered w: Skill 0.40, Impact 0.25, Holds-up 0.15, Consistency 0.20. A component with no detectable player differences gets weight 0 (D30). Effective weights: bat S 40%, I 25%, H 15%, C 20%; bowl S 53%, I 0%, H 20%, C 27%.
why_not_average: Components are on different scales, so each is standardised before weighting.
Small samples are shrunk toward the average first, so 30 lucky balls can't top the list.
Weights were frozen before any ranking existed (pre-registration), never tuned to results.

limitations: Venues are UNKNOWN for all matches (source sites blocked), so there is no venue adjustment.
No external fact could be verified (squads, prices, ages, purse): all are REPORTED, UNKNOWN or [ASSUMPTION].
First-innings win probabilities have little skill beyond the base rate; second-innings ones are informative.
The 2023 model learned from one season (2022) only.
Expected runs from earlier matches trail scoring jumps: mean RAE per ball +0.02 (2023), +0.04 (2024), +0.00 (2025), +0.02 (2026). Season-centred check: top-20 unchanged 100%.
Components with no detectable player differences at these sample sizes (weight 0): bowl match impact (WPA).
Top-10 rankings are too close to call: no pair of top-10 players is separated by their 80% ranges (step4_too_close_to_call).
Backtest: persistence of the score from one season to the next is not demonstrated (small samples; see Method & Proof for hit rates against naive and random-pick baselines).
Fielding is not in the data; wicketkeeper and captaincy are not identifiable.
Ages, injuries and availability are not verifiable here; the shortlist is conditional on the official auction list.
